title: Drummond of Hawthornden helped you at that stile.
html_source:
Scottish poet of the 16th and early 17th centuries, most famous for his “The Cypresse Grove.” He was apparently given to such metaphysical musings as Stephen gives air to here, e.g.,

“This globe of the earth, which seemeth huge to us, in respect of the universe, and compared with that wide pavilion of heaven; is less than little, of no sensible quantity, and but as a point.”

This “stile” of his that Stephen refers to makes frequent use of phrases such as “the All” and “this great All.”
